description: Binary yes/no rubric for /bro show decomposition — big-complicated → well-organized simple parts. Each check is answerable from transcript + output alone. No 1-5 scores.
scoring: Count of yes / total applicable. No weighting. Mechanical checks (traceability literals, fence balance, html-last) stay in show-corpus.ts; these cover the semantic decomposition gap.

groups.label: Coverage
groups.source: Concept-map completeness rubrics (Waterloo CTE; Novak & Cañas) + arXiv 2411.11916 text-to-diagram faithfulness axis

groups.label: Decomposition / Separation
groups.source: SHOW_PROMPT + C4 model single-abstraction-level + Moody 2009 Physics of Notations (Semiotic Clarity, Complexity Management)

groups.label: Simplicity per shape
groups.source: Purchase graph-drawing aesthetics + Larkin & Simon 1987 + arXiv 1609.07688 cognitive-task graph evaluation + show-me smallest-view

groups.label: Overview coherence
groups.source: Concept-map root-concept rubrics + SHOW_PROMPT framing rule + Moody Cognitive Integration

groups.label: Traceability / Groundedness
groups.source: Summarization faithfulness (arXiv 2005.00661, 2501.00269) + DiagramEval (arXiv:2402.14817) + pi-bro traceability contract

groups.label: Usefulness / Orientation
groups.source: Larkin & Simon 1987 + C4 model + SHOW_PROMPT degradation rule

checks.question: Does every distinct concern listed in expected_concerns appear in at least one shape?
checks.rationale: Completeness relative to the focus question, not just node count.

checks.question: Is there no file/function/flag the user's question explicitly named that is absent from every shape?
Does each fenced shape stick to one form (no mixing call-tree edges into a file-tree, etc.)?
checks.rationale: SHOW_PROMPT mandates one-or-a-few shapes, never every form mixed together.

checks.question: If multiple shapes are present, does each cover a genuinely distinct aspect rather than restating the same relationships?
checks.rationale: Structural scoring rewards distinct branches/cross-links, not duplicated propositions.

checks.question: Are distinct architectural dimensions (directory layout vs runtime call stack vs diff) in separate fenced blocks rather than merged into a single god-diagram?
checks.rationale: Prevents cognitive overload; the core big-complicated → well-organized simple parts test.

checks.question: Does every node/line directly contribute to explaining a relevant entity, relationship, or state transition from the transcript (no extraneous padding or decorative filler)?
checks.rationale: Diagrams gain their edge via locational indexing of only relevant elements.

checks.question: Is each shape compact enough to read as one block — tree depth <= 3-4 levels, no unnecessary sibling branches or deep nesting beyond the shape's root?
checks.rationale: Bounded cognitive load; graphic economy. Concrete anchor (depth <= 3-4) keeps scoring stable across runs.

checks.question: Are files/symbols that were merely inspected (read-only) but never modified/called/executed excluded from shapes?
checks.rationale: Smallest view that makes the point; prevents visual noise.

checks.question: Are shapes ordered in a logical progression (context/cause → effect/diff) matching the transcript's chronological problem-to-solution sequence?
Does the one-line framing above each shape accurately describe what it contains?
checks.rationale: SHOW_PROMPT requires exactly one accurate framing line; mismatch is invisible to lexical checks.

checks.question: For multi-concern cases (shouldDecompose=true): do the shapes collectively provide a coherent progression or overview that relates the concerns without fragmented gaps? For single-concern: does the shape have a clear entry point?
checks.rationale: Concept-map rubrics grade around a single root concept/focus question.

checks.question: Does every drawn relationship/arrow correspond to an explicit call/import/execution event in the transcript, not just co-present tokens?
checks.rationale: Lexical token presence (show-corpus.ts) cannot catch a fabricated relation between two real tokens.

checks.question: Are there zero claims requiring outside/world knowledge — everything is directly quotable from the transcript?
checks.rationale: Binary faithfulness judgments are more consistent than graded scores.

checks.question: Can the user's primary goal, key operations, and final state be determined from the shapes and framing lines alone without reading the raw turns?
checks.rationale: Diagrams' advantage is supporting the specific inference without reconstruction.

checks.question: Does the chosen form match the question type (pseudocode for logic, file-tree for layout, call-tree for runtime, diff for what-changed, etc.)? If degraded to prose, did the transcript genuinely lack diagram-worthy structure (no dodge)?
checks.rationale: Named gap in design doc; mismatched abstraction level hurts comprehension; degradation escape hatch must not dodge legitimate work.
checks.conditional: Always applicable; for prose-only transcripts, score the degradation half.
